title: Detecting a large magneto-optical shift in Py/NiO bilayers
authors: Adrielson Dias, Maria Clara, Ozéas Rodrigues, Gabriel Henrique, José Lucas, José Holanda
abstract: Here, magneto-optical magnetometry measurements on Py/NiO bilayers reveal a pronounced magnetic-field-induced wavelength shift, demonstrating strong magneto-optical coupling in this antiferromagnetic system. A systematic and monotonic spectral shift of up to ~ 400 nm is observed as the applied magnetic field increases, saturating at higher fields. Quantitative analysis shows that the associated magneto-optical energy variation is on the order of 107 eV, comparable to the magnon energy scale in NiO. Owing to the large NiO thickness, the observed effect originates from magnons intrinsic to the antiferromagnetic NiO layer rather than from spin currents injected by the Py underlayer. These results provide direct experimental evidence for magnetic-field control of antiferromagnetic magnon energies via magneto-optical interactions, establishing Py/NiO bilayers as a promising platform for optically probing and manipulating antiferromagnetic spin dynamics.
summary: This paper reports on magneto-optical measurements on Py/NiO bilayers, observing a large, field-dependent spectral shift. The findings confirm that this shift arises from the control of antiferromagnetic magnon energies within the NiO layer. This establishes the bilayer as a promising platform for optically probing and manipulating antiferromagnetic spin dynamics.
main_problem: The study aims to detect and characterize a large magneto-optical shift in Py/NiO bilayers, demonstrating strong magneto-optical coupling in an antiferromagnetic system.
main_result: The research provides direct experimental evidence for magnetic-field control of antiferromagnetic magnon energies via magneto-optical interactions in the NiO layer.
method: Magneto-optical magnetometry measurements were performed on the bilayers, analyzing spectral shifts using a laser source and spectrometer.
model_or_system: The physical system is a Py/NiO bilayer, where NiO acts as the antiferromagnetic layer and Py is the ferromagnetic underlayer. The effect is attributed to magnons intrinsic to the NiO layer.
key_observables: Pronounced, systematic, and monotonic spectral shift (wavelength shift) up to ~400 nm, and associated magneto-optical energy variation on the order of 10^7 eV.
important_parameters: The bilayer thickness is Py (20 nm)/NiO (200 nm). The shift saturates at higher applied magnetic fields.
main_assumptions: The observed effect originates from magnons intrinsic to the AF NiO layer, and the contribution from the Py underlayer is negligible due to the large NiO thickness.
figures_summary: Figure 3 shows the wavelength shift induced by the magnetic field in reflectance spectra. Figure 4 compares Raman spectra, showing the shift only in the two-magnon (2M) mode.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical system and measurement setup, presents the observation of the field-dependent spectral shift, analyzes the shift magnitude and origin (confirming magnon control), and concludes by establishing the platform's potential.
why_interesting: The direct experimental control of magnon energies using optical probes and magnetic fields is highly relevant to understanding and manipulating quantum excitations in magnetic materials, which connects to open quantum systems and quantum optics.
